Hello all, I wanted to show this:

Library: https://github.com/nileshtrivedi/lean-detective/blob/main/Detective/Basic.lean
Knives Out: https://github.com/nileshtrivedi/lean-detective/blob/main/Detective/KnivesOut.lean

I built this Lean library that can be used to model criminal investigations, such as murder mysteries. It allows tracking of persons and objects (such as weapons) and their spatio-temporal histories - which is established only after considering unreliable clues and testimonies. I picked Murdle puzzles as the toy versions of this and detective fiction like the movies Drishyam or Knives Out as the harder level. LLMs can easily convert informal narratives into formal, and Lean typechecker can then proof-check proposed conclusions.

It's incredibly fun, because I can choose to model as much of physics and math into my DSL as I'd like. For example, for checking alibis, I can model the physical world either as a graph of cities as discrete nodes for toy problems, or full ℝ^3 in cases where altitude plays a role. I can choose to model Time as a separate variable with LinearOrder, or I can use 4-d Spacetime from PhysLib, for more complex scenarios.

Criminal trials typically follow the MMO framework: Means, Motive and Opportunity. Out of these 3, Motives are the hardest to model in Lean, as it would involve modeling the emotional states of the agents, and a full world simulation in order to represent incentives. This seems hard so motives need to be brought in as hypotheses.
